Neutrons were produced by slamming a 1.6
GeV/c2 proton beam with double bunches per pulse onto
a tungsten target with a typical repetition rate of
25 Hz. The pulse width of each bunch was 41 ns, and
the interval between the two bunches was 410 ns.
A KBr crystal (purity > 99.99%) with a thickness of
2.0 mm, diameter of 30.0 mm, mass of 11.17 g.
A 6LiF-Si detector array with a 360 g/cm2 6LiF
neutron conversion layer and eight separated Si
detectors was used for neutron flux monitoring.
For the RRR, sample-related corrections were included
in the SAMMY analysis. In the URR, multiple neutron
scattering events and self-shielding corrections in
the sample were determined through Geant4 simulations.
